C-BROWSER-SEARCH-PROVIDERS-TARGETING-REP.Summary:
Supersede the stopped execution path of C-BROWSER-SEARCH-PROVIDERS-20260904 after its T-001 feasibility gate exposed a missing generic multi-installation invocation primitive in worldline-kernel.
The functional browser-search scope is unchanged: add an engine-neutral `browser.search/0.1` resolve capability, one ordinary replaceable structured URL-search provider, deterministic S3E proving, and staged Windows real-CEF evidence. The only architectural delta is that explicit provider selection now consumes the applied platform primitive delivered by C-KERNEL-CAPABILITY-PROVIDER-TARGETING-20260905: `CapabilityTarget::Installation(InstallationId)`.
Search resolution remains data-only and separate from browser navigation. Search-provider preference/default selection remains outside the kernel.
C-BROWSER-SEARCH-PROVIDERS-TARGETING-REP.Problem:
The predecessor search plan correctly stopped at T-001 because the generic runtime could discover multiple active installations of one capability but could only invoke the deterministic first compatible provider. That made the second active search-provider installation unreachable without lifecycle manipulation.
C-KERNEL-CAPABILITY-PROVIDER-TARGETING-20260905 has now been applied and archived. The kernel can explicitly route a capability invocation to a durable InstallationId, resolve the current live RuntimeId at admission time, preserve ordinary capability authorization, and fail closed without silently falling back to another provider.
Search can therefore resume without introducing a search-specific router, browser-specific provider registry, kernel preference table, CEF policy, or provider-name branching in consumers.

Goals.Goal: Preserve the approved functional scope and security model of C-BROWSER-SEARCH-PROVIDERS-20260904.
Consume generic InstallationId-targeted capability invocation as the sole explicit multi-installation routing primitive for search-provider selection.
Define additive experimental `browser.search/0.1` resolve semantics without changing stable Browser Contract v1.0.
Keep address/search/command classification in the future shell or caller, not in the search provider.
Implement one ordinary installation-configurable structured URL-search provider that can be installed multiple times with distinct configuration.
Prove an unchanged consumer can invoke installation A or B through generic targeting without provider-name branching.
Keep search-resolution authority disjoint from NavigatePage and all unrelated browser authorities.
Preserve query privacy and bounded structural URL construction.
Prove deterministic S3E and staged Windows real-CEF S3E with loopback-only acceptance.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL AND EXACT PLAN APPROVAL ARE SEPARATE. THIS DRAFT DOES NOT AUTHORIZE IMPLEMENTATION.
C-KERNEL-CAPABILITY-PROVIDER-TARGETING-20260905 MUST REMAIN APPLIED AND ARCHIVED. THIS SEARCH CHANGE MUST NOT MODIFY OR REIMPLEMENT ITS KERNEL PRIMITIVE.
THE PREDECESSOR C-BROWSER-SEARCH-PROVIDERS-20260904 STOPPED AT ITS T-001 FEASIBILITY GATE. IMPLEMENTATION MUST PROCEED ONLY FROM A SUPERSEDING APPROVED PLAN.
EXPLICIT PROVIDER ROUTING MUST USE DURABLE InstallationId TARGETING. DO NOT TARGET RuntimeId DIRECTLY.
IF A TARGET SEARCH INSTALLATION IS ABSENT, STOPPED, QUARANTINED, DEACTIVATING OR INCOMPATIBLE, THE INVOCATION MUST FAIL CLOSED. NO SILENT FALLBACK TO ANOTHER SEARCH PROVIDER.
THE KERNEL PROVIDES ROUTING MECHANISM ONLY. SEARCH DEFAULTS, USER PREFERENCES AND PERSISTENT PROFILE POLICY MUST NOT ENTER worldline-kernel.
SEARCH IS AN ORDINARY REPLACEABLE PLUGIN CAPABILITY. NO SEARCH VENDOR, OMNIBOX, QUERY-TEMPLATE OR DEFAULT-PROVIDER DOMAIN POLICY MAY ENTER worldline-kernel OR CEF.
`browser.search/resolve` MUST NOT NAVIGATE, OPEN WINDOWS, EXECUTE SCRIPT, MUTATE DOM, READ COOKIES/STORAGE, START DOWNLOADS OR EXERCISE BROWSER MUTATION AUTHORITY.
SEARCH RESOLUTION AND browser.navigate ARE SEPARATE AUTHORIZED CAPABILITY INVOCATIONS.
EVENT BUS IS NOT RPC. SEARCH RESOLUTION RETURNS THROUGH NORMAL CAPABILITY REQUEST/RESULT FLOW.
THE FIRST PROVIDER MUST BUILD URLS STRUCTURALLY FROM A PARSED FIXED WEB ORIGIN/PATH, ONE VALIDATED QUERY PARAMETER, AND BOUNDED STATIC PARAMETERS. RAW QUERY STRING CONCATENATION IS FORBIDDEN.
PRODUCTION TARGETS MUST USE HTTPS. HTTP IS ALLOWED ONLY FOR EXPLICIT LOOPBACK TEST CONFIGURATION. javascript:, data:, file:, about: AND OTHER EXECUTION/LOCAL-RESOURCE SCHEMES ARE FORBIDDEN.
QUERY TEXT, STATIC PARAMETER VALUES AND RESULT URLS MUST HAVE FINITE DECLARED BOUNDS. OVERSIZED VALUES FAIL EXPLICITLY WITHOUT BROWSER MUTATION.
RAW QUERY TEXT MUST NOT ENTER GENERIC METRICS, TRAJECTORY PAYLOADS, PANIC/DEBUG TEXT OR UNRELATED EVENTS BY DEFAULT.
PROVIDER FAILURE MUST DEGRADE SEARCH ONLY. DIRECT URL NAVIGATION AND EXISTING M1.3 SERVICES MUST REMAIN AVAILABLE.
NO PUBLIC INTERNET DEPENDENCY IS ALLOWED IN ACCEPTANCE TESTS. REAL CEF EVIDENCE USES LOOPBACK AND THE PINNED/STAGED RUNTIME.
NON-WINDOWS WORKSPACE COMPILATION MUST REMAIN GREEN; REAL CEF S3E MAY BE WINDOWS-ONLY WITH EXPLICIT Unsupported/Unavailable ELSEWHERE.
GRACE PROJECTIONS ARE NOT APPLIED UNTIL FRESH COMPLETION EVIDENCE AND EXPLICIT OWNER APPLY CONFIRMATION.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Kernel preferred-provider tables or search-specific routing policy.
Choosing a permanent default search vendor.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The applied kernel targeting primitive is treated as baseline and no search implementation changes worldline-kernel.
Two simultaneously active installations exposing the same search capability can be invoked independently through InstallationId targeting by unchanged consumer logic.
Target unavailability is typed and fail-closed with zero silent fallback.
An experimental engine-neutral `browser.search/0.1` contract exists with one bounded resolve request and bounded SearchNavigationTarget result; navigation is outside the contract.
Search-resolution authority is disjoint from NavigatePage, ActOnPage, page observation, cookies, storage, downloads, request policy and DevTools authorities.
A search-only principal can resolve a target but receives AccessDenied when attempting normal browser navigation.
`worldline-browser-search` supports multiple installations with distinct installation-owned structured URL configuration and no provider-vendor enum in the consumer contract.
Search text changes only the designated query-parameter value and cannot alter scheme, credentials, authority, hostname, port, path, fragment or static parameter keys.
Unicode, spaces, reserved characters, percent signs and query/fragment-looking text are encoded deterministically without structural escape.
Production configuration rejects non-HTTPS remote targets, userinfo, malformed hosts, forbidden schemes, empty query parameter names and oversized configuration/results.
Raw query text is absent from generic metrics, trajectory payloads, panic/debug text and unrelated events in acceptance evidence.
Deterministic S3E proves provider A and B produce distinct expected loopback targets for the same input with unchanged consumer code.
Search resolution alone causes zero loopback origin hits; a later separately authorized browser.navigate causes exactly the expected hit with the decoded query value.
Hosted/staged Windows real-CEF S3E uses the normal native provider process, rejects ReferenceBrowserBackend substitution and proves the same resolve-then-navigate composition.
Search-provider unload/replacement/crash/quarantine/unavailability does not break direct navigation or existing M1.3 service proving slices.
Architecture guards prevent search vendor/configuration policy from entering worldline-kernel/CEF and prevent worldline-browser-search from becoming a dependency of unrelated services.
A BrowserSearch CI gate covers contract bounds, generic InstallationId targeting, authority separation, privacy, structured URL safety, deterministic S3E and staged real-CEF S3E.
Existing Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, ProvingSlice, RealChromium, BrowserProvider, BrowserServices, BrowserRequestPolicy, BrowserDevTools, RealS3B and All gates are preserved.
Completion evidence distinguishes scaffolded, wired and verified claims and does not apply graph/verification projections before explicit owner confirmation.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh evidence names the applied kernel targeting baseline, selected InstallationId and resolved RuntimeId topology, authority separation, deterministic URL encoding and bounds, provider replacement/failure behavior, query privacy, zero-origin-hit proof before navigation, separately authorized loopback navigation, real staged CEF provider identity and preserved existing browser-service gates.

Assumptions.Assumption: C-KERNEL-CAPABILITY-PROVIDER-TARGETING-20260905 remains applied and archived and its acceptance tests stay green.
The first useful web-search capability only resolves already-classified text to a navigation target.
A structured fixed base URL plus one query parameter and bounded static parameters covers the first proving providers.
Existing browser.navigate and real-CEF loopback infrastructure can consume the resolved target without a browser-engine search primitive.
Search provider configuration is installation-owned state and does not need to enter stable Browser Contract v1.0.
